The changes in `fnic_fcs.c` enhance the functionality by reducing unnecessary log messages, ensuring that the port speed is only logged when it changes, which addresses the issue of log spamming. The correction in `fnic_trace.c` improves the clarity of the log message regarding the port speed, ensuring that the information presented to the user is accurate and free of typographical errors. Together, these changes improve the overall logging behavior and accuracy of the driver.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
shost_printk(KERN_INFO, fnic->lport->host, "Current vnic speed set to :  %llu\n",
			(u64)atomic64_read(
			&fnic->fnic_stats.misc_stats.current_port_speed));
```
Reason:
The above code executes unconditionally in the `fnic_handle_link` function, causing the vnic port speed to be printed to syslog every time `fnic_handle_link` is called (which is every 2 seconds for link events), leading to excessive log entries and spamming.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (old_port_speed != new_port_speed)
	shost_printk(KERN_INFO, fnic->lport->host,
				"Current vnic speed set to :  %llu\n",
				new_port_speed);
```
Reason:
The fix introduces a conditional check that only logs the current vnic speed if it has changed (`old_port_speed != new_port_speed`). This prevents the log messages from being printed repeatedly and limits logging to instances where the port speed actually changes or during driver initialization, thereby eliminating the spamming issue in syslog.
